rooms.name: Pump Room
rooms.description: A shift bell hangs over an idle iron pump. A return wire vanishes through the bars of the north arch.

encounters.cue: A brass key hangs under the pump spout.
encounters.result: The key lifts off the hook. Its bit fits the north grate.
encounters.hint: The brass key is already in your pocket.

encounters.cue: The north grate has a keyhole bleached green by the water.
encounters.result: The brass key turns. The grate swings clear of the north arch.
encounters.hint: Take the brass key from the pump spout to unlock the grate.

changes.text: Three knocks answer the bell through the pipe. The middle knock comes twice.
The lowest pipe finally falls quiet. Dust from the new lake road whitens the pump housing.
The iron pump draws from a full lake. Small handprints in dried mud lead uphill from the arch.
For every pump stroke, another answers on the return pipe. The bell hangs still between shifts.
The iron grate is swung back against the stone, leaving the north arch open.

rooms.name: Grotto
rooms.description: Amber water laps against the arch. A wet bell wire runs up to the landing, vibrating long after the sound has died.

encounters.cue: Trace the groove beneath the wet bell wire.
encounters.result: The wire has worn two grooves into the arch. In the deeper one a twist of red wool still keeps the metal from ringing against stone.

rooms.name: Bell Landing
rooms.description: The bell rope ends here in a child's leather mitten. Mara keeps the other mitten tied around her wrist.

encounters.cue: Mara, last surface keeper, winds a mitten string round her thumb. She cares who rang the bell.
encounters.result: Mara names the doubled middle knock: her sister Ada taught it to her. Bring the two shift names from the roll vault to the pilot bell to call the crew.

replies.text: Mara puts her ear to the empty pipe. She can hear the footsteps of people walking across the lakebed.
Mara starts writing the families’ names in the keeper’s book, leaving space for the old street names.
Mara sets two places at the change of shift. One is for the keeper from below.

encounters.cue: Tell Mara what Ada said about the other mitten.
encounters.result: Mara fits her mitten over the bell pull. When her sister taps, she taps back with both hands.
encounters.hint: Talk to Mara here and find Ada at her window in the lantern borough.

changes.text: The bell rope wears both a mitten and a fresh ribbon. Mara and Ada share the pipe again.

rooms.name: Boot Rack
rooms.description: Pairs of boots stand toes out, ready for a shift that never came up. One small pair has odd blue stitching around both toes.

encounters.cue: Turn over the smallest pair of boots.
encounters.result: The soles are strips of ferry sail. Blue stitching follows the old sail seam right around the toes.

rooms.name: Lamp Issue
rooms.description: Brass hooks numbered by shift hold empty lamps. Someone has recently collected wick number forty-one.

encounters.cue: Examine the hook for wick forty-one.
encounters.result: A fresh twist of wick has snagged on the burr. Someone took the lamp down recently enough for the wax to smell of tallow.

rooms.name: Key Bench
rooms.description: Old wax impressions show the north grate key slowly wearing smooth under generations of thumbs.

encounters.cue: Hold the wax impressions side by side.
encounters.result: The teeth hardly change between casts. It is the bow, where a keeper waited with a thumb through it, that wore thin.

rooms.name: Intake Mouth
rooms.description: A tin cup on a chain tastes of fresh water for the first mouthful and brine for the second.

encounters.cue: Inspect the links on the drinking cup.
encounters.result: Two links are flattened bright at the rim. One dips the cup just below the fresh layer, the other into the brine beneath.

rooms.name: Flywheel Well
rooms.description: A wheel taller than a cottage turns a finger's width with each knock. Light from the grotto flashes through one missing spoke.

encounters.cue: Look into the empty spoke socket.
encounters.result: The broken end is filed smooth and painted white. Even without a clock the keepers could count revolutions in the dark.

rooms.name: Oil Niche
rooms.description: Rags smell of walnut oil. One has been wrapped round the bell wire to keep it from cutting the stone.

encounters.cue: Unfold a corner of the rag around the wire.
encounters.result: The hem is embroidered with a tiny loaf. A kitchen towel became a bearing when the stores ran out of felt.

rooms.name: Pipe Choir
rooms.description: Each copper pipe sings a different pitch. The lowest note travels toward the weeping locks.

encounters.cue: Compare the collars on the singing pipes.
encounters.result: A different number of rivets stands proud on each collar. A listener could identify a silent pipe by touch.

rooms.name: Meal Shelf
rooms.description: A slate gives the price of bread in wick ends. Somebody has rubbed out the old price and doubled it.

encounters.cue: Read the faded marks at the edge of the price slate.
encounters.result: A child's drawing shows a heel of bread beside a burnt wick. The smallest portion was measured against a child's hand.

rooms.name: Whistle Booth
rooms.description: A cracked speaking trumpet points down. A return pipe, labelled for replies, still brings warm air up.

encounters.cue: Inspect the mouth of the return pipe.
encounters.result: A hammered copper funnel bears tooth marks on its rim. Someone below held it steady while both hands were busy.

rooms.name: Counterweight Pit
rooms.description: Iron teeth bite into the guide rail. Red wool has caught on a tooth far above the present weight.

encounters.cue: Examine the red wool caught on the rail.
encounters.result: A narrow woven stripe remains in the yarn. It matches the warning bands painted at shoulder height along the pit.

rooms.name: Rain Court
rooms.description: Rain falls through a square of open sky into a bucket marked as city property. The overflow belongs to the people below.

encounters.cue: Look under the city bucket's spout.
encounters.result: A second lip has been soldered on with kitchen tin. It sends the overflow cleanly into a pail directly below.

rooms.name: Chain Stair
rooms.description: Pairs of bright marks on the handrail show where stretchers once swung on the descent.

encounters.cue: Measure the distance between the bright marks.
encounters.result: The marks come in pairs a stretcher-width apart. At every landing a wider pair shows where the bearers changed hands.

rooms.name: Time Clock
rooms.description: Every brass tag is punched IN. None of the matching OUT holes has been cut.

encounters.cue: Look inside the clock's OUT slot.
encounters.result: The punch is sharp beneath the dust. The missing checkouts cannot be blamed on a broken cutter.

rooms.name: Muster Gate
rooms.description: The gate lists three destinations in enamel: the records office, the locks and the ferry. A new arrow beside the old lettering points down.

encounters.cue: Examine the new arrow on the gate.
encounters.result: A strand of lampwick clings to the last stroke. Whoever painted the arrow had a wick to hand and no brush.

rooms.name: Porter's Cot
rooms.description: The mattress was slit open to make bandages. Its ticking hangs in washed strips by the hot pipe.

encounters.cue: Compare the strips of ticking by the pipe.
encounters.result: The ends have little cuts one palm apart so cloth could be torn to length with one free hand.

rooms.name: Ash Culvert
rooms.description: Pale flakes drift from the kiln district. They cling to the damp roof in the shape of many small hands.

encounters.cue: Look closely at the hand-shaped gaps in the ash.
encounters.result: The same bent little finger appears again and again. One small person felt along this roof for quite a distance.

rooms.name: Survey Nail
rooms.description: A copper nail marks the last height the city and the lower town agreed on. The present stain is a thumb above it.

encounters.cue: Examine the washers behind the copper nail.
encounters.result: Two washers bear different seals, one a gate and one an oar. Both banks once signed off on the same water mark.
